media.alt: Combating the process and the diseases of ageing

content.text: "If we live long enough, all of us will experience deterioration in our bodily functions, of different types and to different degrees," informed Dr Tom Martin, Consultant Obstetrician and Chief of Obstetrics and Gynaecology of the Aga Khan University Hospital (AKUH). He was giving a presentation on "Combating the Process and the Diseases of Ageing" at "Signs, Symptoms and Care", a monthly public health awareness program, held on June 26, 1999 at AKUH. Dr Martin added that "many of us develop heart diseases, cancer, etc. and the development of diseases associated with ageing can be combated or avoided by modifications of lifestyle and of diet".

Highlighting the importance of regular exercise and food intake, Dr Martin revealed that by adopting a proactive lifestyle the process of ageing could be retarded. He further informed that around 10 percent-80 percent of women as they would grow older will develop signs and symptoms due to hormone deficiency. These troublesome symptoms occur just before and after menopause and can be avoided with the use of hormones. Dr Martin stressed on the usage of Hormone Replacement Therapy (HRT) in menopausal women to prevent occurrence of serious diseases, such as heart diseases, bone diseases, etc.
A panel of Consultant Gynaecologists also participated in the panel discussion, which included Dr Rahat Najam Qureshi and Dr Nasreen Chaudhury.
